classification.difficultyReason: Convert ten minutes to hours and use speed × time to obtain the actual distance, read five centimetres from the grid, then compare the distances to justify the supplied scale. This links motion, units and map interpretation through routine methods.

content.prompt:
A map is drawn to scale, on 1-cm paper, showing the position of a supermarket and a cinema.

It takes 10 minutes to walk in a straight line from the cinema to the supermarket at a constant speed of 3 km/h. Show that the scale of the map is $1\text{ cm}=100\text{ m}$.

spec.description: Seven-column, two-row square grid with Cinema on the first internal vertical line and Supermarket on the sixth, both on the middle horizontal line. A blank-grid template cannot express the required labelled point markers.
spec.mathematics: Each grid interval represents 1 cm on the map. The points are five horizontal intervals apart, so their map distance is 5 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: The grid, both points and both labels are permanent student-visible givens; no solution marks are included.

answer.short: The actual distance is $500\text{ m}$ and the map distance is $5\text{ cm}$, so $1\text{ cm}$ represents $100\text{ m}$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Time}&=\frac{10}{60}\text{ h}=\frac16\text{ h}\\\text{Actual distance}&=3\times\frac16\text{ km}\\&=0.5\text{ km}\\&=500\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
The points are five grid intervals apart, so their map distance is $5\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Distance represented by }1\text{ cm}&=\frac{500}{5}\text{ m}\\&=100\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
Hence the scale is $1\text{ cm}=100\text{ m}$.
